title: Spiral Galaxies NGC 5905 & NGC 5908
caption: The spiral galaxies NGC 5905 and NGC 5908, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector/University of Alaska Anchorage, H. Schweiker/WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Two spiral galaxies share this view in the constellation Draco. NGC 5905, in the upper-right corner, faces us directly, while NGC 5908 in the lower left is turned edge-on. The two are relatively close to each other in space.

The contrast shows how much our viewing angle matters. A face-on spiral displays its arms like a pinwheel, while an edge-on spiral appears as a narrow band, often crossed by a lane of dust. NGC 5908 closely resembles M104, the famous Sombrero Galaxy.

Scattered across the image are many bright, reddish stars. These stars have nothing to do with the two galaxies. They belong to our own Milky Way and simply lie in the foreground, between us and the much more distant galaxies.

understand.summary: The Mosaic camera on the Mayall 4-meter Telescope used three filters. B is shown in blue, V in green and I in red.
filters: 438 nm · Optical B (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
538 nm · Optical V (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
820 nm · Optical I (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
understand.eye: These galaxies are far too faint for the eye, and the I filter records near-infrared light we cannot see.
